newsitem.title: USA: Hastings says auto strikes could hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Hastings says auto strikes could hurt Q2.

text.p: Hastings Manufacturing Co said Friday new products and accounts are helping offset sales delays from strikes at several automotive plants, but a prolonged strike could hurt second-quarter sales.
"A prolonged strike by automotive workers could have a negative impact on second-quarter sales," Hastings said in a statement.
Workers at various auto plants, including General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp, have been on strike in recent weeks, and other walkouts are threatened.

On Friday Hastings, which provides piston rings, specialty tools and engine additives, reported first quarter earnings of $0.55 a share on revenues of $8.75 million versus $0.41 on $11.36 million last year.

The company said the revenue decline was due to discontinued sales of filter products following the company's sale of the business. Excluding filter sales, Hastings said its core product sales rose 1.3 percent for the quarter.

"While sales of these core products were up only slightly versus a year ago, we laid important groundwork for the future during the first quarter of 1997," Mark Johnson, co-chief executive, said in a statement.

"Strong new account activity in North America and the continued diversification of our overseas distributor network are putting Hastings in position to increase sales of our branded Hastings and Casite products," he said.

The company said the change in product mix and recent restructuring pushed margins higher. Gross profit increased to 32.3 percent of sales in the first quarter 1997, compared with 26.9 percent for the same period last year.

"Moving forward, we will continue to emphasize cost management as well as a strong sales effort and innovative new products that leverage our brand names and distribution channels," Andrew Johnson, co-chief executive, said.
